questions.question: As per India Skills Report 2022, which Indian state got the first rank with the most employable talent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the India Skills Report 2022, **Maharashtra** ranked first among Indian states with the most employable talent.
 
• The state has consistently shown strong performance in nurturing and developing employable skills among its workforce.
 
• The survey covered a wide range of parameters including educational background, skill development initiatives, and industry readiness.
 
• Maharashtra's robust educational infrastructure and numerous skill development programs have significantly contributed to its top ranking.
 
• The state has a high number of institutions offering vocational training and higher education, which play a crucial role in enhancing employability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India Skills Report**

 
 
• The India Skills Report is an annual report that assesses the employability of the Indian workforce based on various parameters.
 
• It is a collaborative effort by Wheebox, the Association of Indian Universities (AIU), Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), and other partners.
 
• The report provides insights into the gap between the skills possessed by the workforce and the skills required by industry.
 
• It serves as a useful tool for policymakers, educational institutions, and industry stakeholders in making informed decisions.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development Initiatives in India**
 
 
• The Government of India has launched several initiatives to enhance skill development, including the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).
 
• These initiatives aim to improve the employability of the youth by providing industry-relevant skill training.
 
• There are also sector-specific skill councils that work towards addressing the skill gaps in various industries.
 
• Such initiatives play a critical role in aligning the skill development efforts with the needs of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Vocational Education and Training (VET)**
 
 
• VET focuses on equipping individuals with practical skills required in specific trades or professions.
 
• It includes formal and informal training and is critical for workforce readiness in various industries.
 
• VET programs are designed to meet the demands of the labor market, thereby improving the employability of participants.
 
• Countries with robust VET systems tend to have lower youth unemployment rates and a more skilled workforce.
 
 
 
• **Higher Education and Employability**
 
 
• Higher education institutions play a pivotal role in developing the skills and competencies of graduates.
 
• There is an increasing emphasis on integrating skill development programs within higher education curricula.
 
• Industry-academia partnerships are crucial for ensuring that the education system meets the evolving demands of the job market.
 
• Internships, apprenticeships, and hands-on training are effective methods to bridge the gap between education and employment.

questions.question: Baishagu is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Baishagu is a prominent festival celebrated by the Bodo tribe in Assam.
 
• This festival marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year and is celebrated during the mid-April.
 
• Baishagu involves traditional dance forms such as the Bwisagu dance, performed to the tunes of traditional musical instruments.
 
• The festival is characterized by rituals that honor the local deities and ancestors, as well as community feasting and merrymaking.
 
• It is one of the most vibrant and significant cultural festivals in Assam, reflecting the rich heritage of the Bodo community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bodo Tribe:**

 
 
• The Bodos are one of the largest ethnic and linguistic groups in Assam, belonging to the Bodo-Kachari community.
 
• They speak the Bodo language, which is recognized as one of the 22 scheduled languages of India.
 
• The Bodo people primarily inhabit the Bodoland Territorial Region in Assam.
 
 
 
• **Assamese New Year:**
 
 
• The Assamese New Year, also known as Rongali Bihu, is celebrated in mid-April.
 
• It marks the beginning of the agricultural cycle, especially the onset of the sowing season.
 
• Rongali Bihu is a time of joy and festivities, involving traditional music, dance, and feasts.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Music and Dance:**
 
 
• The Bwisagu dance is performed during Baishagu with traditional Bodo musical instruments like kham (drum) and sifung (flute).
 
• Dance and music are integral parts of the festival, showcasing the cultural richness of the Bodo community.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Festivals like Baishagu play a crucial role in preserving and promoting the cultural heritage of indigenous communities.
 
• They foster community bonding and provide an opportunity to pass traditions and customs to younger generations.

questions.question: What do you mean by ‘cant’ in kabaddi?

options.text: A player in whose court a raid is made
A special point is given to an opponent
A player who enters the court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Repeating round of the word 'kabaddi'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In kabaddi, 'cant' refers to the continuous chanting of the word 'kabaddi' during a raid.
 
• The raider must repeat the word 'kabaddi' without breaking the chant to demonstrate that they are not holding their breath.
 
• The chant acts as a timer for the raid; the raider must return to their half of the court before running out of breath.
 
• Failing to maintain the chant or taking a breath results in the raider being declared out.
 
• This rule ensures that the raider does not stay in the opponent's court for an extended period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kabaddi**

 
 
• It is a contact team sport that originated in ancient India.
 
• The game involves two teams of seven players each, who take turns sending a "raider" into the opposition's half to tag out as many defenders as possible.
 
• Points are scored by the raider for each opponent tagged, while the opposing team tries to capture the raider.
 
 
 
• **Raid**
 
 
• A raid is the primary action in kabaddi where one player (the raider) enters the opponent's half to tag out players.
 
• The raider must return to their half within 30 seconds while maintaining the 'cant'.
 
• If the raider gets caught and cannot return, the opposing team scores a point.
 
 
 
• **Defense**
 
 
• The defending team tries to stop the raider by tackling or catching them.
 
• If the raider is stopped and unable to return, the defending team earns a point.
 
• Defensive strategies include forming chains or circles to trap the raider.
 
 
 
• **Super Tackle**
 
 
• A super tackle is when three or fewer defenders tackle the raider successfully.
 
• It awards two points to the defending team instead of one.
 
• This strategy is crucial when the defending team is outnumbered.

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest atomic power plant of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tarapur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tarapur Atomic Power Plant (TAPP) is the oldest nuclear power plant in India, established in 1969.
 
• It is located in Tarapur, Maharashtra, about 140 kilometers north of Mumbai.
 
• The plant was built with the help of the United States under the 1963 Indo-US nuclear cooperation agreement.
 
• Initially, the plant had two boiling water reactors (BWRs) with a capacity of 160 MW each, which were later upgraded.
 
• Tarapur Atomic Power Station is currently operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nuclear Power in India**

 
 
• India's nuclear power program aims to secure energy independence, utilizing its vast thorium reserves.
 
• The Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) oversees the country's nuclear energy production.
 
• As of 2023, India has 22 operational nuclear reactors in 7 nuclear power plants, with a total installed capacity of 6780 MW.
 
• Major nuclear power plants include Kudankulam, Kaiga, Kakrapar, Narora, and Rawatbhata.
 
 
 
• **Indo-US Nuclear Cooperation**
 
 
• The 1963 agreement led to the establishment of the Tarapur plant and laid the foundation for future nuclear cooperation.
 
• The Indo-US Civil Nuclear Agreement signed in 2008 further facilitated India's access to nuclear technology and fuel.
 
 
 
• **Boiling Water Reactor (BWR)**
 
 
• A BWR is a type of nuclear reactor that uses light water as both a coolant and a neutron moderator.
 
• In BWRs, water is boiled to produce steam directly in the reactor core, which then drives the turbine generator.
 
• Tarapur's initial reactors were BWRs, making it unique among India's nuclear reactors.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL)**
 
 
• NPCIL is a public sector enterprise under the DAE, responsible for designing, constructing, and operating nuclear power plants.
 
• It plays a crucial role in India's nuclear power generation and the implementation of advanced nuclear technologies.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in Article 19 of the Constitution of India?

options.text: To reside and settle in any part of India
To practice any profession or occupation
To prohibit ineligibility in respect of employment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To prohibit ineligibility in respect of employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 19 of the Constitution of India guarantees certain fundamental freedoms to the citizens of India.
 
• These freedoms include the right to freedom of speech and expression, the , the right to form associations or unions, the right to move freely throughout the territory of India, the right to reside and settle in any part of India, and the right to practice any profession or occupation.
 
• The right "To prohibit ineligibility in respect of employment" is not included in Article 19.
 
• Article 19 specifically deals with the protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
 
• The right to equality in matters of employment is covered under Article 16 of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 19**

 
 
• Article 19(1) guarantees six freedoms to the citizens of India.
 
• These freedoms are subject to reasonable restrictions laid down by the state in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the state, public order, decency, or morality.
 
 
 
• **Article 16**
 
 
• Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence, or any of them.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution of India.
 
• They are justiciable, which means they are enforceable by the courts.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**
 
 
• These principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution of India.
 
• They are non-justiciable, which means they are not enforceable by the courts.
 
• They are fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to establish a just society.

questions.question: Where is the secretariat of the Goods and Services Tax Council located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Secretariat of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council is located in **New Delhi, India**.
 
• The GST Council Secretariat was established to assist the GST Council in the discharge of its functions.
 
• It plays a crucial role in coordinating between the central government and various state governments regarding GST matters.
 
• The Secretariat provides administrative and logistical support for the GST Council meetings and other related activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**

 
 
• GST is an indirect tax that has replaced many indirect taxes in India such as excise duty, VAT, services tax, etc.
 
• It is a single tax on the supply of goods and services, right from the manufacturer to the consumer.
 
• GST is a destination-based tax, meaning it is collected from the point of consumption rather than the point of origin.
 
• There are three types of GST in India: CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), and IGST (Integrated GST).
 
 
 
• **GST Council**
 
 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body for making recommendations to the Union and State Governments on issues related to GST.
 
• The Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes the Union Minister of State for Finance and the Finance Ministers of all the states.
 
• Decisions in the GST Council are taken by a three-fourth majority of the votes cast, with the central government having one-third of the votes and the state governments having two-thirds.
 
 
 
• **GST Network (GSTN)**
 
 
• GSTN is a non-profit organization established to manage the entire IT system of the GST portal, which is the common and shared IT infrastructure between the central and state governments, taxpayers, and other stakeholders.
 
• It facilitates the registration, payment, and return filing processes under GST.
 
• GSTN ensures data security and confidentiality of taxpayer information.
 
 
 
• **Impact of GST**
 
 
• GST has simplified the tax structure by subsuming various indirect taxes under a single regime.
 
• It has helped in reducing the cascading effect of taxes, thereby lowering the overall tax burden on goods and services.
 
• GST has improved the ease of doing business by providing a common national market and reducing complexities related to tax compliance.

questions.question: Some of the features of Samudragupta are shown on Satavahana coins, one of which shows him playing the ______?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Veena.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The ruler of the Samudragupta, which is known as the golden age of India, has achieved significant achievements in the arts, literature and sciences during this period.
 
• He is filmed to play Veena on his coins, which reflects his interest and skill in music.
 
• Veena is a traditional Indian instrument that has been used in different forms for thousands of years.
 
• This filming represents the cultural and artistic attitude of the sea, not only the warrior he has learned, but also a patron of the arts.
 
• The rule of the sea is particularly recognized for blossoming scientific Indian music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Gupta clan:
 
• The Gupta clan is about 320 to 550 CE. Ruled up to and considered the highest level of ancient Indian civilization.
 
• This period is known for its great achievements in various fields, including arts, architecture and sciences.
 
• The Gupta Empire has a large portion of the Indian subcontinent and is famous for its culture and practices.
 
• Indian classical music:
 
• Indian classical music is divided into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Karnataka (South Indian).
 
• Veena is a prominent instrument in both traditions, but it is more common in Carnatic music.
 
• Indian classical music is based on tunes (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic wheels).
 
• Coins in ancient India:
 
• Coins are not just a medium of exchange, but also the propaganda path that the rulers use their power and achievements.
 
• Gupta coins are specifically identified for their artistic quality and the information they provide about that period.
 
• Films on coins often contain images of rulers, gods and wealth.
 
• ​Veena:
 
• Veena is one of the oldest Indian music instruments, and there are indications that return to ancient texts such as Vedas.
 
• It has a large, resonant body and is played by plucking the strings by pressing them on the fretboard.
 
• There are a variety of veins such as Saraswati Veena, Rudra Veena and Strange Veena.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest, double membrane-bound organelles, which contain all the cell’s genetic information?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The nucleus is the largest double membrane-bound organelle present in eukaryotic cells.
 
• It contains the cell's genetic information in the form of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid).
 
• The double membrane is called the nuclear envelope, which has nuclear pores to allow the exchange of materials between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
 
• The nucleus plays a crucial role in cell division and controls various cellular activities by regulating gene expression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chromatin:** The genetic material in the nucleus exists as chromatin, a complex of DNA and proteins, which condenses to form chromosomes during cell division.
 
• **Nucleolus:** A prominent structure within the nucleus, it is the site of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis and ribosome assembly.
 
• **Nuclear Envelope:** The double-layered membrane that encloses the nucleus, separating its contents from the cytoplasm.
 
• **Nuclear Pores:** These are large protein complexes that span the nuclear envelope, allowing the transport of molecules between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
 
• **Functions of the Nucleus:** It regulates gene expression, stores genetic information, and coordinates cell activities such as growth, metabolism, and reproduction.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a central bank’s function?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banking facilities for the public**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Central banks primarily regulate and supervise the financial system, rather than providing direct banking facilities to the general public.
 
• Commercial banks are responsible for offering banking services such as savings accounts, personal loans, and other financial products to the public.
 
• Central banks focus on maintaining monetary stability, controlling inflation, and managing the nation's currency.
 
• They also act as a lender of last resort to commercial banks to ensure liquidity and stability in the financial system.
 
• Central banks provide financial services to the government and manage the country's foreign exchange and gold reserves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary Policy:**

 
 
• Central banks implement monetary policy to control inflation, manage employment levels, and stabilize the currency.
 
• They use tools like interest rates, open market operations, and reserve requirements to influence the economy.
 
 
 
• **Lender of Last Resort:**
 
 
• Central banks act as a lender of last resort to provide liquidity to commercial banks during financial crises.
 
• This helps prevent bank runs and ensures the stability of the financial system.
 
 
 
• **Currency Issuance:**
 
 
• Central banks have the exclusive authority to issue national currency and regulate its supply.
 
• This includes managing the design, production, and distribution of banknotes and coins.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Exchange Management:**
 
 
• Central banks manage the country's foreign exchange reserves and intervene in the forex market to stabilize the currency.
 
• They also facilitate international trade and maintain balance of payments stability.

questions.question: Which Treaty resulted in the demarcation of territories between Ranjit Singh and the East India Company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amritsar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Treaty of Amritsar was signed between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and the British East India Company on April 25, 1809.
 
• This treaty clearly demarcated the boundaries between the territories controlled by Ranjit Singh and those under the British East India Company.
 
• The treaty prevented Ranjit Singh from expanding his territory south of the Sutlej River.
 
• It established a mutual understanding that neither party would interfere in the territories of the other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maharaja Ranjit Singh:**

 
 
• Ranjit Singh was the founder and leader of the Sikh Empire in the early 19th century.
 
• He successfully unified the various Sikh factions into a powerful kingdom in the Punjab region.
 
 
 
• **British East India Company:**
 
 
• An English company formed for the exploitation of trade with East and Southeast Asia and India, incorporated by royal charter on December 31, 1600.
 
• It eventually came to rule large areas of India with its own private armies, exercising military power and assuming administrative functions.
 
 
 
• **Sutlej River:**
 
 
• A major river in the Punjab region that flows through both India and Pakistan.
 
• Its strategic significance made it a natural boundary in various historical agreements.
 
 
 
• **Treaties and Agreements:**
 
 
• Such treaties were common during the colonial era to establish control and influence over regions.
 
• They often involved negotiations to prevent conflicts and ensure smoother administration of the territories.

questions.question: Capital market is a market for ________ funds.

options.text: both short term and long term

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**long term**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The capital market is primarily focused on **long-term investments**.
 
• It facilitates the **buying and selling** of long-term financial instruments such as stocks, bonds, and other securities.
 
• Institutions like **stock exchanges** and **bond markets** are integral parts of the capital market.
 
• The capital market helps in the **allocation of resources** and **economic growth** by channeling savings into productive investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Market:**

 
 
• Deals with the issuance of new securities directly from the issuers to investors.
 
• Includes Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) and private placements.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Market:**
 
 
• Involves the trading of existing securities among investors.
 
• Includes stock exchanges where securities are bought and sold.
 
 
 
• **Equity Market:**
 
 
• Part of the capital market where shares are issued and traded.
 
• It is also known as the stock market.
 
 
 
• **Debt Market:**
 
 
• Part of the capital market where debt instruments like bonds are traded.
 
• It helps in raising funds for governments and corporations.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Bodies:**
 
 
• Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates the capital markets in India.
 
• Ensures transparency, fairness, and investor protection.

questions.question: As per Article 350 B of the Constitution of India, who appoints the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 350 B of the Constitution of India deals with the appointment of a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
 
• The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The role of the Special Officer is to investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution.
 
• The Special Officer reports directly to the President on the status and issues faced by linguistic minorities in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 29 and 30**

 
 
• Article 29 provides that any section of citizens residing in the territory of India having a distinct language, script, or culture have the right to conserve the same.
 
• Article 30 grants linguistic and religious minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
 
 
• **National Commission for Minorities**
 
 
• It is a statutory body established to safeguard the rights of minorities in India.
 
• The commission addresses issues related to minority rights and welfare.
 
 
 
• **Language in the Constitution**
 
 
• Part XVII of the Constitution deals with the official language of the Republic of India.
 
• It outlines the use of Hindi and English in official government communications.
 
 
 
• **Protection of Linguistic Rights**
 
 
• Various provisions in the Constitution aim to protect the linguistic rights of minorities, ensuring they are not discriminated against based on language.
 
• These measures include education in mother tongue and the establishment of linguistic minority commissions.

questions.question: NITI Aayog came into existence in 2015. On which date was it formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1st January**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• NITI Aayog, the National Institution for Transforming India, was formed on **1st January 2015** by the Government of India.
 
• It replaced the **Planning Commission**, which was established in 1950.
 
• The formation of NITI Aayog was part of the government's effort to better adapt to **changing economic conditions** and provide a more flexible and agile framework for planning and policy-making.
 
• It was created to serve as a **policy think tank** of the Government of India and foster cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Composition of NITI Aayog**

 
 
• Chairperson: The Prime Minister of India.
 
• Governing Council: Comprising the Chief Ministers of all the States and Lt. Governors of Union Territories.
 
• Regional Councils: Formed to address specific regional issues, chaired by the Prime Minister or his nominee.
 
• Full-time organizational framework includes a Vice-Chairperson, Members, and Chief Executive Officer (CEO).
 
 
 
• **Objectives of NITI Aayog**
 
 
• To promote cooperative federalism through well-defined support initiatives and mechanisms with the States.
 
• To foster a shared vision of national development priorities, sectors, and strategies with the active involvement of States.
 
• To design strategic and long-term policy frameworks and programs and review their progress and efficacy.
 
• To provide advice and encourage partnerships between key stakeholders and national and international like-minded think tanks, as well as educational and policy research institutions.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives by NITI Aayog**
 
 
• **Aspirational Districts Programme**: Aims to rapidly transform districts that have shown relatively less progress in key social areas.
 
• **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)**: A flagship initiative to promote a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship in the country.
 
• **Digital India**: A campaign launched to ensure the Government's services are made available to citizens electronically by improving online infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Difference from Planning Commission**
 
 
• Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not have the power to allocate funds to the states.
 
• NITI Aayog emphasizes on bottom-up approach rather than the top-down approach of the Planning Commission.
 
• Focuses more on fostering cooperative federalism and involving states in the planning process.

questions.question: Name the place where “independent” parallel government by Indians was established during the Quit India movement as a mark of revolt against British government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the Quit India Movement of 1942, parallel governments were formed in several parts of India as an act of defiance against British rule.
 
• **Satara** in Maharashtra was notable for establishing a parallel government, often referred to as the "Patri Sarkar."
 
• This government was led by local leaders such as Krantisinh Nana Patil, who played a significant role in its formation and operation.
 
• The Satara parallel government took over the administration, implemented its own laws, and provided services to the local populace, effectively functioning as an independent entity for a period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quit India Movement:**

 
 
• The Quit India Movement, also known as the August Movement, was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8th August 1942 at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee (AICC).
 
• It demanded an end to British rule in India and was marked by widespread acts of defiance, including strikes, protests, and the establishment of parallel governments.
 
 
 
• **Patri Sarkar (Satara Parallel Government):**
 
 
• The term "Patri Sarkar" translates to "Rebel Government" and it was established in Satara district to provide an alternative to British rule.
 
• The parallel government collected taxes, settled disputes, maintained law and order, and conducted welfare activities.
 
 
 
• **Krantisinh Nana Patil:**

• **Charles Elton's Contributions**

questions.question: What kind of image does the eye lens form of the object on the retina?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The eye lens forms an inverted image of the object on the retina.
 
• This image is real, meaning it can be projected on a screen.
 
• The retina, which is located at the back of the eye, acts as the screen where the image is formed.
 
• The brain processes this inverted image and perceives it as upright.
 
• The process of forming an image on the retina is essential for vision.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Retina:**

 
 
• The retina contains light-sensitive cells called rods and cones.
 
• Rods are responsible for vision in low light conditions, while cones are responsible for color vision and detail.
 
 
 
• **Lens:**
 
 
• The lens is a transparent, flexible structure that can change shape to focus light on the retina.
 
• This process of changing shape is called accommodation.
 
 
 
• **Optic Nerve:**
 
 
• The optic nerve transmits visual information from the retina to the brain.
 
• It consists of over a million nerve fibers.
 
 
 
• **Ciliary Muscles:**
 
 
• These muscles control the shape of the lens.
 
• They relax or contract to change the lens' curvature for focusing.
 
 
 
• **Visual Cortex:**
 
 
• The visual cortex is the part of the brain that processes visual information.
 
• It interprets the signals from the optic nerve to create the perception of vision.

• **Liberalisation** refers to the process of reducing government restrictions and regulations in an economy to enhance the ease of doing business and promote economic activities.
 
• This typically involves **reducing tariffs, trade barriers, and government monopolies**, and allowing greater competition and private sector participation.
 
• The primary aim is to **increase economic efficiency and stimulate growth** by allowing market forces to determine prices and production.
 
• Countries often implement liberalisation policies to attract **foreign investment** and improve their competitiveness in the global market.
 
• Examples of liberalisation include the **privatisation of state-owned enterprises** and deregulation of industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privatisation:**

 
 
• It involves the transfer of ownership of property or businesses from a government to a privately owned entity.
 
• Privatisation is often used to increase efficiency and productivity in the economy.
 
• Examples include the sale of government stakes in companies to private investors.
 
 
 
• **Deregulation:**
 
 
• It refers to the removal or simplification of government rules and regulations that constrain the operation of market forces.
 
• The goal is to increase the efficiency of markets and reduce the costs of compliance for businesses.
 
• Deregulation can be seen in sectors like airlines, telecommunications, and financial services.
 
 
 
• **Globalisation:**
 
 
• It is the process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
 
• Globalisation is often facilitated by liberalisation policies that open up economies to foreign trade and investment.
 
• It can lead to greater economic integration and interdependence among countries.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms of 1991:**
 
 
• India introduced significant economic reforms in 1991, which marked the beginning of liberalisation in the country.
 
• Key reforms included reducing trade tariffs, deregulating industries, and encouraging foreign direct investment (FDI).
 
• These reforms were aimed at making the Indian economy more market-oriented and expanding the role of private and foreign investment.

questions.question: Which of the following movements is included in volcanism?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Volcanism refers to the processes through which molten rock (magma) and gases are expelled from the earth's interior onto its surface.
 
• Molten rock, or magma, plays a key role in volcanic activity and can form various types of volcanic landforms when it cools and solidifies.
 
• When magma reaches the surface, it is known as lava, which can flow and create extensive lava plains or build up into volcanic mountains.
 
• Volcanism is a significant geological process that contributes to the formation of new crust and the recycling of old crust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Volcanic Eruptions**

 
 
• Effusive Eruptions: Characterized by the outpouring of lava onto the ground.
 
• Explosive Eruptions: Resulting in the violent ejection of volcanic ash, tephra, and gases.
 
 
 
• **Volcanic Landforms**
 
 
• Shield Volcanoes: Broad, gently sloping landforms created by low-viscosity lava flows.
 
• Stratovolcanoes: Steep, conical mountains formed by alternating layers of lava and tephra.
 
• Calderas: Large depressions formed when a volcano collapses after a massive eruption.
 
 
 
• **Major Volcanic Zones**
 
 
• Ring of Fire: A major area in the Pacific Ocean basin where many earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur.
 
• Mid-Atlantic Ridge: A mostly underwater mountain range in the Atlantic Ocean where new oceanic crust is formed.
 
 
 
• **Volcanic Hazards**
 
 
• Lava Flows: Can destroy infrastructure and alter landscapes.
 
• Volcanic Ash: Can affect air travel, human health, and agriculture.
 
• Pyroclastic Flows: Fast-moving currents of hot gas and volcanic matter that can be deadly.

questions.question: Which of the following committees observed that “essentially all that is contained in the fundamental duties is just a codification of tasks integral to the Indian way of life”?

__
 
• The Verma Committee was established to address and provide recommendations on amending laws to deal with sexual assault cases.
 
• In its report, the Verma Committee emphasized that fundamental duties are essentially a codification of tasks integral to the Indian way of life.
 
• The committee was named after its chairman, Justice J.S. Verma, former Chief Justice of India.
 
• The committee submitted its report on 23 January 2013, suggesting several legal and administrative reforms.
 
• It played a crucial role in shaping the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, which strengthened laws against sexual violence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties in Indian Constitution**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• They were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• There are 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• Often called the "Mini-Constitution" due to its comprehensive nature.
 
• It introduced several changes, including the addition of Fundamental Duties and changes to the Preamble.
 
• It shifted the balance of power towards the center and curtailed the powers of the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013**
 
 
• Also known as the Nirbhaya Act, it was passed in response to the 2012 Delhi gang rape case.
 
• The Act introduced stringent penalties for crimes like rape, sexual harassment, and acid attacks.
 
• It also broadened the definition of rape and made provisions for faster trials and increased victim support mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Justice J.S. Verma**
 
 
• Served as the 27th Chief Justice of India from 1997 to 1998.
 
• Known for his integrity and significant contributions to Indian judiciary reforms.
 
• He chaired the Verma Committee, which brought transformative changes in laws pertaining to women's safety.

questions.question: Which of the following area pair of barrel-shaped organelles located in the cytoplasm of animal cells near the nuclear envelope, which give orientation to the 'mitotic spindle' formed during cell division?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centrioles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Centrioles are a pair of barrel-shaped organelles located in the cytoplasm of animal cells near the nuclear envelope.
 
• They play a crucial role in the organization of the mitotic spindle during cell division.
 
• Each centriole is composed of nine sets of microtubule triplets arranged in a cylindrical form.
 
• Centrioles help in the formation of cilia and flagella, which are structures involved in cell movement and signaling.
 
• During mitosis, centrioles duplicate, and the pairs move to opposite poles of the cell to assist in the segregation of chromosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centrosome**

 
 
• The centrosome is the main microtubule organizing center of the cell and is composed of two centrioles.
 
• It regulates the cell's cytoskeleton and is vital for the integrity of cellular processes.
 
• During cell division, the centrosome duplicates to ensure each daughter cell inherits one centrosome.
 
 
 
• **Mitotic Spindle**
 
 
• The mitotic spindle is a structure composed of microtubules that segregates chromosomes into the daughter cells during mitosis.
 
• Spindle fibers are crucial for the accurate separation of chromosomes.
 
• The spindle apparatus originates from the centrosomes.
 
 
 
• **Microtubules**
 
 
• Microtubules are tubular structures that provide structure and shape to cells.
 
• They are composed of tubulin proteins and are integral to many cellular processes, including vesicle transport and cell division.
 
 
 
• **Cell Division**
 
 
• Cell division is the process by which a parent cell divides into two or more daughter cells.
 
• It is essential for growth, reproduction, and repair in multicellular organisms.
 
• There are two types of cell division: mitosis and meiosis.

questions.question: Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal) is targeted at sustainable ________ management.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**groundwater**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal) is a central sector scheme of the Government of India aimed at sustainable management of **groundwater resources**.
 
• The scheme was launched on **25th December 2019** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• It is implemented by the Ministry of Jal Shakti and funded by the Government of India and the World Bank.
 
• Atal Bhujal Yojana focuses on areas with critical and over-exploited groundwater resources, covering **seven states**: Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The primary goal of the scheme is to promote **community-led** sustainable groundwater management, involving local communities and stakeholders in its execution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Groundwater Depletion**

 
 
• Groundwater depletion refers to the long-term reduction in the quantity of groundwater stored in aquifers.
 
• It is primarily caused by excessive extraction for agricultural, industrial, and domestic purposes.
 
• Consequences include reduced water supply, increased pumping costs, and land subsidence.
 
 
 
• **Aquifers**
 
 
• Aquifers are underground layers of water-bearing rock or materials such as gravel, sand, or silt.
 
• They store groundwater and release it to wells or springs.
 
• Aquifers can be confined or unconfined based on their geological characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Water Conservation Techniques**
 
 
• Water conservation techniques include rainwater harvesting, efficient irrigation methods, and wastewater recycling.
 
• Drip irrigation and sprinkler systems are effective methods to reduce water usage in agriculture.
 
• Rainwater harvesting involves collecting and storing rainwater for reuse, reducing dependency on groundwater.
 
 
 
• **Community Participation**
 
 
• Community participation in water management involves engaging local stakeholders in decision-making processes.
 
• It ensures sustainable and equitable distribution of water resources.
 
• Successful groundwater management requires active involvement of communities in monitoring and conservation efforts.

questions.question: Megasthenes, a Greek, was the ambassador in the court of which of the following kings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta Maurya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by Seleucus I Nicator, a Hellenistic king.
 
• He visited the Mauryan Empire around 302-298 BCE.
 
• Megasthenes is best known for his work "Indica," which provides a detailed account of India during Chandragupta Maurya's reign.
 
• His observations and writings are one of the primary sources of information about the Mauryan Empire and its society.
 
• Megasthenes' accounts highlight the administrative efficiency and infrastructure of the Mauryan Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya**

 
 
• He was the founder of the Maurya Empire and ruled from 321 to 297 BCE.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya established a vast empire that extended across northern and central India.
 
• He is known for his centralised administration and the establishment of a bureaucratic system.
 
• His advisor, Chanakya (Kautilya), wrote the Arthashastra, an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft and economic policy.
 
 
 
• **Seleucus I Nicator**
 
 
• He was one of Alexander the Great's generals and founded the Seleucid Empire.
 
• After Alexander's death, Seleucus established control over large areas of the former Macedonian Empire in Asia.
 
• He engaged in diplomacy and established relations with Indian rulers, including Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• Seleucus exchanged ambassadors with Chandragupta, which led to Megasthenes' visit to India.
 
 
 
• **Indica by Megasthenes**
 
 
• Indica is a historical account that describes the geography, culture, and political structure of India during the Mauryan period.
 
• Although the original text of Indica is lost, fragments of the work have been preserved in the writings of later authors like Arrian, Strabo, and Diodorus.
 
• Megasthenes' observations provide valuable insights into the life and society of ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Administration**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire had a highly organized and efficient administrative system.
 
• It was divided into provinces, each governed by a viceroy appointed by the emperor.
 
• The empire maintained a large standing army and a network of spies to ensure internal security.
 
• The administration focused on infrastructure development, including roads, irrigation, and trade routes.

questions.question: Which of the following earthquake waves is more destructive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surface waves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Surface waves are seismic waves that travel along the Earth's surface and are typically the most destructive type of seismic wave during an earthquake.
 
• They have larger amplitudes and longer durations compared to body waves, leading to more significant ground movement.
 
• Surface waves are divided into two main types: Love waves and Rayleigh waves.
 
• Love waves cause horizontal shifting of the ground, while Rayleigh waves cause a rolling motion, similar to ocean waves.
 
• Because of their higher amplitude and lower frequency, surface waves cause more damage to buildings and infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Body Waves**

 
 
• These are seismic waves that travel through the Earth's interior.
 
• They are divided into Primary (P) waves and Secondary (S) waves.
 
• P-waves are compressional waves that travel fastest and can move through both solid and liquid layers of the Earth.
 
• S-waves are shear waves that travel slower than P-waves and can only move through solid materials.
 
 
 
• **Primary Waves (P-Waves)**
 
 
• P-waves are the first waves to be detected by seismographs during an earthquake.
 
• They cause particles in the ground to compress and expand in the direction of wave propagation.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Waves (S-Waves)**
 
 
• S-waves are slower than P-waves and arrive after them.
 
• They cause particles in the ground to move perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation, resulting in a shearing motion.
 
 
 
• **Seismograph**
 
 
• A seismograph is an instrument used to detect and record earthquakes.
 
• It measures the motion of the ground and helps in determining the location and magnitude of an earthquake.
